A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SelfSplat and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends after its references; v4 includes supplementary Sections A-D. The retained material and additions support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 2-8 report original novel-view synthesis, pose estimation, cross-dataset generalization, and ablation results on RE10k, ACID, and DL3DV.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds efficiency measurements, multiple-context-view experiments, DTU evaluation, additional baseline comparisons, and encoder ablations.

M1.justification: The encoders, feature fusion, matching-aware pose network, depth refinement, and training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix A supplies implementation details, while the additional context-view experiments test the existing model without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained RE10k, ACID, and DL3DV evaluations, v4 adds out-of-distribution evaluation on DTU object scenes. Appendix B.2 also evaluates three and four context views over longer sequences and measures camera-trajectory reconstruction, substantially extending domain and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Table 12 introduces evaluated comparisons with Splatt3R, pixelSplat, and MVSplat on DTU. Table 13 adds VAE and DBARF to cross-dataset comparisons that previously included only FlowCAM and CoPoNeRF. The original comparator sets remain present.

E3.justification: New protocols measure peak memory and inference time for 256-by-256 images on an RTX 4090, and evaluate three/four context views over 80/120 frames using Absolute Trajectory Error. Section 5.1 also changes overlap thresholds from percentage notation to fractions. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The original component and loss ablations remain. Table 14 adds tests removing CroCo initialization, the monocular encoder, and the multi-view encoder. Additional analyses examine inference cost, scaling to more context views and longer trajectories, and rendered depth quality, substantially expanding the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The supplementary results continue point-estimate reporting; the retained pose-error means and medians are not run-to-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2-8 are unchanged, but v4 adds substantial numerical and qualitative evidence in Tables 10-14 and Figures 8-14. For example, DTU PSNR is 13.14 for SelfSplat, 10.24 for Splatt3R, 12.89 for pixelSplat, and 13.94 for MVSplat. These are new comparisons with differing training or pose requirements, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an explicit first-order spherical-harmonic expression and permutation matrix for color-coordinate warping. The original mathematical definitions, objectives, and pose-gradient expression in Equations 1-11 remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about pose-free and 3D-prior-free reconstruction, reciprocal benefits of self-supervision and Gaussian splatting, and cross-dataset generalization. The supplement adds supporting evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations of efficiency and multi-view scalability, and attributes Splatt3R's DTU scale inconsistencies to pretrained metric geometry and intrinsic-parameter differences. It also explains the choice of self-supervised initialization. The earlier limitations concerning wide-baseline reconstruction and dynamic scenes are retained in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents encoder initialization, frozen-backbone adapters and dimensions, spherical-harmonic order, optimizer settings, batch sizes, training budgets, hardware, frame sampling, and evaluation splits. It also explains baseline adaptations and DL3DV initialization. These substantially improve documentation without establishing changes to the underlying retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds PF3plat and No Pose, No Problem alongside GGRT and revises discussion of pretrained-model dependencies. Appendix B.3 positions SelfSplat against Splatt3R and pose-required Gaussian methods. Additional supporting references broaden coverage while preserving the original research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain nearly identical. Changes include author and affiliation edits, limited related-work and evaluation wording revisions, an organized supplement, and relocation of the limitations and project link. There is little rewriting of the retained scientific exposition.

P2.justification: The original figures and tables remain with small layout adjustments. v4 adds Tables 9-14 and Figures 7-14, including a detailed architecture diagram, trajectory plots, DTU and depth comparisons, and extensive qualitative galleries. This substantially expands the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 fills substantial reproducibility gaps through its training, implementation, and sampling details. New encoder ablations, measured efficiency, trajectory tests, and DTU comparisons make important aspects of the unchanged method more assessable. DTU comparisons remain qualified by differing training and pose requirements, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the gains in documentation and empirical scrutiny substantially improve the paper.
